punchline: "I would definitely buy that" sounds like a sale and tells you only the speaker's mood.
thirty_sec: Rob Fitzpatrick says customers give you three kinds of bad data: compliments, fluff and ideas. Compliments are fool's gold. Fluff is "I always", "I would", "I might". The cure is the same each time: skip the opinion and ask about the last time the problem actually happened, and why they want the feature they asked for.
